entry.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
entry.summary:
Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two successive contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations in Katriel's differential-equation model, but no chaos. We derive from the elementary reactions of the process, without reference to the differential equations, a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $τ$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_τ$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $τ\to0$.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #complex-systems
